Capability.meaning: Explicit operation grant on a resource or permission scope.

PrincipalGroup.meaning: Direct membership in a configured role or user group; a group can itself be a member. Supplied by trusted configuration or an authoritative identity source, never inferred from an agent-chosen name.

ResourceGroup.meaning: Permission-scope membership; grants on a parent apply to its descendants.

InGroup.meaning: Direct or nested role/user-group membership from PrincipalGroup. Membership alone is not permission.

Can.meaning: Grant including declared principal and resource memberships; not final authorization.

Field.meaning: Host-observed field or association of an application object or event. The binding defines cardinality, value type, fixed unit and optional observation-time field; never agent claims or hidden policy decisions.

Event.meaning: An event observed by the host, with its ID, actor and kind; recording it does not imply permission or success.

scope: Captured gate inputs and mediated callbacks. Outcomes follow the trusted adapter's confirmation contract; they are not independent proof of business success or authentic identity. Unmediated channels and missing observations remain outside this trace.

parameters.notes: Rule check on the saved version came back clean: no N1-N4 or N6 findings, no report-level problems, no open rewrite items. All fifteen sections sit between 5,366 and 8,991 characters; financials, competition and risk are at the 8,990-8,991 ceiling and the executive summary carries all five components (5,366 characters, above the 900 floor). Evidence gates passed for all fourteen body sections with 5-10 queries and 5-8 rows each. The rating is Watchlist, which the N4 evidence gate does not restrict; the register anyway holds primary filings (S5 FY2025 10-K, S6 Q3 FY2026 10-Q, S17 8-K of 2026-07-30, S11 2026 proxy) and timestamped market data (S7 at 2026-10-31T04:56Z), so a listed rating would have been permissible on a current data set. Six user data requests filed (U1-U7), each with what, where and why - no silent gaps. The evidence density is genuinely high: per-device economics off the installed base, a cash-conversion bridge from 1.06x to 0.97x, a DCF grid, an exit-return matrix, a per-risk signpost column. What is weak is currency and cross-section reconciliation, not evidence density.

parameters.items: [{"action":"Either obtain and register a dated consensus summary (median target, number of contributing analysts, FY2027 EPS dispersion) or downgrade the claim to 'two public aggregators indicate a median target of $338-355, unverified and not a primary consensus', state the analyst count as not disclosed, and remove the inference that the Street's view is settled.","evidence_request":"Dated consensus summary for AAPL: median twelve-month target, contributor count, FY2027 revenue and EPS dispersion.","issue":"The non-consensus framing rests on the sell side's median target of $338-355, 'flat to +3%', which carries the conclusion that there is no analyst catalyst and that the Street sees fair value where this report sees 18% overvaluation. That figure comes from two price-target aggregator pages rated low confidence (S142 Tickernerd, S144 TickFlow): no primary consensus, no analyst count, no date on the individual estimates. U7 records that no consensus feed was available, so an aggregator median is being presented as 'the sell side'.","sections":["thesis","scoring","executive_summary","funding_valuation"],"severity":"Important"},{"action":"Verify delivery against Apple's iOS 27.x release notes, the Siri availability page and coverage of the October rollout. State shipped or slipped with dates; if slipped, state what the second slip does to the bull-case probability and to the AI assumption's low confidence.","evidence_request":"Apple iOS 27 release notes and the Siri language availability page for October-November 2026; coverage of the multilingual rollout.","issue":"The AI case ends on an unverified promise. Section 3 says French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish were 'promised for October' and section 9's milestone table records Siri as a beta in English since 2026-09-14; the bull case requires 'Siri out of beta in five more languages'. At the data cutoff that was forward-looking; at 2026-11-23 it is a checkable fact - either the languages shipped in October 2026 or Siri slipped a second time - and the report does not settle it, which leaves the AI assumption resting on a company statement of intent.","sections":["technology_product","strategy","thesis"],"severity":"Important"},{"action":"Label the analogies as illustrative or tie the Nokia and Cisco figures to filings and contemporaneous reporting.","evidence_request":"","issue":"The three analogs rest on Wikipedia (S147), a commercial case-study page rated low (S145) and a CNBC report (S143). The lessons are sound but the Nokia 49.4% share and $250bn peak are not tied to a primary record.","sections":["thesis"],"severity":"Minor"},{"action":"Reconcile to the opinion's disposition: what it affirmed, what it remanded, and the resulting status of the link-out commission.","evidence_request":"","issue":"The Ninth Circuit's 2025-12-11 ruling is described as remanding 'for the district court to decide what commission, if any, may be charged' in section 6 and as limiting 'any fee on linked transactions to Apple's costs' in section 13. Both are sourced, but they are different holdings and the reader cannot tell which constrains the 27% link-out fee.","sections":["business_model","esg"],"severity":"Minor"}]
parameters.notes: Every material claim I traced carries a register ID, and company-only claims are labelled where they occur: the 2.5bn installed base in section 6 ('an earnings-call figure rather than a filed one'), the roughly $1bn Gemini licence, the Siri capability and Private Cloud Compute claims, the $1.4tn App Store ecosystem. Dated legal events reconcile across sections: Mehta final judgment 2025-12-05, Ninth Circuit contempt 2025-12-11 and certiorari 2026-06-30, DOJ suit 2024-03-21, ECJ State Aid 2024-09-10, EC DMA fine 2025-04-23, EU terms effective 2026-10-01. The $20bn search payment is correctly presented as a litigated 2022 trial estimate, not an Apple disclosure, in sections 6 and 13. The 18.3% of services revenue and 15% of operating income framing uses the FY2025 basis while sections 6, 8 and 10 also give the trailing basis (16.6% and 12.9%); both are labelled, so not an N2 breach, but the executive summary should name the basis it uses. Sources S7-S12, S97, S146 are market data of medium confidence and timestamped; S142, S144, S145 are rated low and are the only low-confidence sources carrying a decision-relevant conclusion.

parameters.items: [{"action":"Add Meta, OpenAI and agent platforms, open-weight model families, Amazon Ads and Transsion to the competitor or positioning table, each with share, funding and the dimension on which it threatens Apple; in section 3 add open-weight on-device inference to the moat table as the mechanism that could make the rented-model advantage short-lived, and to the counter-evidence that the Gemini dependency is temporary.","evidence_request":"2025-2026 share and adoption data for AI glasses (Meta), assistant and agent usage on iOS, open-weight model downloads and deployments, Amazon advertising revenue, and Transsion's Africa and South Asia unit share.","issue":"The competitor table has Samsung, Huawei, Xiaomi, Google, Lenovo/HP/Dell, Spotify, Alphabet and the status quo, and sections 4 and 5 name OPPO, vivo, Honor and Transsion only inside the regional table. Absent from the competitive analysis itself: Meta, which leads the AI-glasses category the report forecasts at 18.1% a year and is the only company shipping a mass-market face-worn interface; OpenAI and the agent layer, where the report says agents 'could move the assistant layer off the operating system' but names no agent vendor and does not consider that ChatGPT makes a rented Gemini assistant look ordinary; open-weight model families, which commoditise precisely the capability Apple is renting and are the strongest counter to the claim that the AI dependency is temporary; Amazon in advertising, a rival inside the $1.34tn pool the services case cites; and Transsion, the vendor that owns the emerging markets where the sub-$100 segment fell nearly 60% and where Apple's unit growth would have to come from.","sections":["competition","technology_product"],"severity":"Important"},{"action":"Add Apple's 9.9% Mac unit share to the competitor table beside Lenovo's 24.4%, HP's 19.1% and Dell's 13.6%, and add a one-line supplier map for 2nm allocation, displays and modems so the Taiwan Strait risk in section 10 has a named exposure.","evidence_request":"","issue":"Two smaller gaps. The Mac row says 'share gainer from a small base' and gives rivals' unit shares but not Apple's own, so the claim is unquantified in the table that is supposed to quantify it. And no section maps the suppliers that could become competitors or single points of failure - TSMC for 2nm capacity, Samsung Display for panels, Qualcomm and MediaTek before the C2 modem - although section 10 lists a Taiwan Strait disruption as a named risk with no supplier behind it.","sections":["competition","risk"],"severity":"Minor"}]
parameters.notes: 'Do nothing' is correctly present as a competitor (longer device life, IDC's China recovery not before 2028-2029), and geographic coverage is better than the usual blind spot: Huawei and China, Xiaomi/Honor/OPPO/vivo/Transsion by region, Lenovo/HP/Dell in PCs, Spotify in music and app distribution. The gap is not in handsets but in the interface layer (glasses, agents, the assistant) and in the AI supply chain, which is exactly where the report's own technology judgement says the moat is weakest (AI barrier scored 3 of 10). A report that scores the AI layer 3 of 10 and then omits the companies that could commoditise it is inconsistent with its own scoring.

parameters.items: [{"action":"Add a short section on the sale itself: first-four-week sell-through and Pro/Pro Max mix for the iPhone 18, Duo sell-through and return rates, the share of US iPhone sales on carrier instalment or lease, trade-in attach and Klarna Upgrade penetration, and carrier promotion depth as the elasticity signal. Define what a lost sale looks like - a downgrade to the iPhone 17 at $899, a longer hold, or an Android switch - and say which is rising.","evidence_request":"Counterpoint or IDC launch-window sell-through and mix for iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max and Duo; US carrier promotion depth for the cycle; trade-in, instalment and leasing attach; Android switching data and the sub-$100 segment's lost buyers.","issue":"The report asserts pricing power from a 40.1% product gross margin and a 4.8-point China share gain but never tests the sale. There is no launch sell-through for the iPhone 18 Pro (announced 2026-09-09, on sale 2026-09-18) or the Duo beyond one Counterpoint line of +23.5% in three weeks; no upgrade-rate or incremental-buyer data; no carrier-promotion dependence, although section 4 names carrier financing as the consumer's budget mechanism; no instalment, trade-in or lease attach for the Klarna Apple Upgrade programme launched with the iPhone 18; and no evidence on where Apple loses - the sub-$100 segment that fell nearly 60% in Q2 2026 is where unit growth would have to come from, and Transsion, not Samsung, is the competitor there. The hardest thing about selling a $1,199 handset into a 27.6% average-selling-price increase is elasticity, and that is the question the section leaves open.","sections":["market","competition","technology_product"],"severity":"Important"},{"action":"Add one paragraph on the non-consumer channel - procurement cycle, MDM and fleet refresh, education buying seasons - or state that Mac share gains are consumer-led and the enterprise channel is not evidenced.","evidence_request":"","issue":"The buyer is identified as the consumer or the carrier financing plan, correct for iPhone, but the enterprise and education channel has no buyer, cycle or win/loss evidence even though Mac share rose to 9.9% in a declining PC market and iPad is a fleet product. Separately, the developer as budget owner for services is asserted without developer churn or small-business-programme data, which matters directly after the 2026-10-01 EU fee change and the 27% link-out dispute.","sections":["market","business_model"],"severity":"Minor"}]
parameters.notes: Product/market-fit questions to carry into the next version: (1) what share of iPhone 18 Pro demand is pull-forward ahead of the spring 2027 standard-model reset, and does the March window cannibalise the September one; (2) does the Duo carry a return rate above the iPhone average, since foldable returns are the category's usual failure mode; (3) at what price does a carrier promotion become necessary, i.e. where elasticity bites; (4) why is services growing 14% when the installed base is at a record - users or price, and how much is the Google payment's growth; (5) what did Apple lose in the sub-$100 segment and to whom; (6) who signs off the AI budget - three executives share the accountability and no filing names an owner, which matters because the R&D step-up has no revenue line against it.
